hints: Focus on what adding two molecules of HBr to two C=C bonds must do, each double bond gains one H and one Br.
Work out where the two Br atoms can end up on the four-carbon chain to give three different skeletons, think 1,4- versus 1,3- versus 2,3-.
Test each dibromobutane for a carbon joined to four different groups to decide which ones can be chiral.
walkthrough:
**Understand the addition**

Think of 1,3-butadiene as $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. Each $\text{C}=\text{C}$ is consumed by one HBr.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + 2\text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{Br}_2$$
So each original double bond gets one H and one Br.

**List the three structural isomers**

For the left $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$, either C1 gets Br or C2 gets Br. For the right $\text{C3}=\text{C4}$, either C3 gets Br or C4 gets Br. Combining gives three distinct skeletons.

$$\text{BrCH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2\text{Br (1,4-dibromobutane)}$$
$$\text{BrCH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHBr}-\text{CH}_3 \text{ (1,3-dibromobutane)}$$
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CHBr}-\text{CHBr}-\text{CH}_3 \text{ (2,3-dibromobutane)}$$

**Test each for a chiral centre**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups attached. Check each structure carefully.

1,4-dibromobutane has no such carbon, both ends are $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ and middles are $\text{CH}_2$. 1,3-dibromobutane has C3 joined to H, Br, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. 2,3-dibromobutane has C2 and C3 each joined to H, Br, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CHBrCH}_3$. So two products have at least one chiral centre.

options.A: Incorrect. Two of the dibromobutanes do contain carbons with four different substituents, so the count is not zero.
options.B: Incorrect. Both 1,3-dibromobutane and 2,3-dibromobutane are chiral, so more than one product qualifies.
options.C: Correct. The three products are 1,4-dibromobutane (achiral), 1,3-dibromobutane (C3 is chiral) and 2,3-dibromobutane (C2 and C3 are chiral centres). Hence 2 products have at least one chiral centre.
options.D: Incorrect. This trap assumes all three dibromides are chiral. 1,4-dibromobutane, BrCH2CH2CH2CH2Br, is symmetrical with only CH2 groups and has no chiral centre.
